rounds.text: The most damning risk facing Orissa Minerals Development Company Ltd is the staggering overhang of contingent liabilities, which stand at an enormous Rs. 6,061 Cr against a market capitalisation of just ₹ 2,266 Cr [E2, E48]. This colossal legal or financial exposure dwarfs the entire enterprise value of the firm, creating an unquantifiable tail risk for shareholders. Compounding this vulnerability is a severe debt burden, with borrowings ticking upward to Rs. 211.90 Cr while the company simultaneously suffers from a low interest coverage ratio [E29, E47]. Furthermore, capital allocation is currently bleeding free cash flow, which plummeted to Rs. -40.81 Cr in Mar 2026 even as capital-work-in-progress expanded by 68.1% to Rs. 186.75 Cr, signaling a heavy cash drain during its capex build-up phase [E27, E30]. Market sentiment reflects deep underlying distress, with the stock trading well below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, burdened by a miserable relative-strength rating of 11 and a devastating historical drawdown of -93.7% [E37, E38, E40]. Institutional capital is actively fleeing the counter, confirming negative money flow and a low rules-based screen score of 43 out of 100 that denotes low confidence and neutral fundamentals [E34, E50]. Conceded: [E12].
